summary: Retest of the iteration-4 minor fixes. Backend: 68/68 pytest pass (13 new in test_iter5_invoice_fixes.py plus the existing suites; the iter4 docs-row assertion was updated to the INV series). Verified: INV###### sequential POS invoice series (cash, card, last split share; cancelled and unpaid orders get none; Zomato orders get none), the monthly docs row (from INV000001, total = count, cancelled = 0, summary.cancelled_invoices >= 1), the demo store backfill (INV000001..INV000015, 15 issued), whole-number rates in the B2CS/HSN CSVs ('5', '18'), the cancel guard (400 for Paid and Partial POS orders; Pending can still be cancelled), and the double-pay guard ('Share already paid' 400; 6 concurrent pays of one share or one order give exactly one 200). Found one remaining race: when two DIFFERENT last shares are paid at the same time, invoice numbers are skipped (5 gaps in 30 runs; the pytest case failed 1 time in 15). UI: MoveTableDialog (a Free target moves at once; a busy target shows merge-confirm-bar, and the API confirmed T4 was still Occupied before confirm; cancel hides the bar; confirm merges, T2 = Rs 504), MonthlyGst (gst-load-error on a 500 with the export button disabled; fast prev/next with a slow stale response shows the correct month's data; a CSV 500 shows an 'Export failed' toast; download works), and ReceiptPrint shows 'Invoice # INV000015' after a cash checkout. The 'Bill split into N shares' toast is removed (code-verified).

minor.issue: Paying the last 2 split shares at the same time: both requests see all_paid=True and both call _assign_invoice. Both requests increment db.counters, but only one $set lands, so a number is skipped (reproduced 5 times in 30 runs with /app/backend/tests/race_probe.py). This breaks the 'no gaps' rule for GSTR-1 Docs Issued (to - from + 1 != total). The same race could also let a late 'Partial' write overwrite 'Paid' (not seen in 30 runs).

action_items: Fix the invoice gap race: only the request that actually changes payment_status to Paid should take a number. For example: res = update_one({id, payment_status: {$ne: 'Paid'}, splits: {$not: {$elemMatch: {status: 'Pending'}}}}, {$set: {payment_status: 'Paid'}}), and call _assign_invoice only if res.modified_count == 1. Also, in _assign_invoice, claim the order before incrementing the counter (or set invoice_no with a filter so the counter is incremented only once per order).
Write the Partial status with a filter on payment_status != 'Paid' so a late Partial write cannot overwrite Paid.
critical_code_review_comments: _assign_invoice increments the counter before its conditional $set, so any duplicate call skips a number. The early-return check is not atomic.
The backfill_invoices filter is channel == 'POS', so older orders with no channel field are skipped (_assign_invoice itself defaults to POS). Consider {channel: {$nin: ECO_CHANNELS}}.

Docs-issued uses orders created in the month, but invoice numbers are assigned at payment time. A bill opened on the last night of a month and paid after midnight is counted in the earlier month. This is low impact.
server.py is about 1318 lines; consider splitting it into routers (payments, reports, tables).
